cases.note: The address read apart: its path, segments, the segments below the space, its query.
Outside a space the template segments are the whole path, and there is no space path.
"~/x" goes from the template’s root, the space it is mounted under.
A record id goes in the query, written so it reads back exactly.
"?q" is the page on screen with that query.
".." from the root route stays at the root: a template cannot climb out of its space that way.
An absolute path leaves the template.
Going to the page on screen changes nothing and says nothing.
One query parameter written; the path is unchanged.
null removes the parameter.
Writing the value a parameter already holds changes nothing and says nothing.
With push, the write is a history entry of its own: Back returns to the query before it.
Back goes to the entry before, query and all.
Going to another space carries the section across when that space has it, and its sections follow.
A section the destination does not have is not carried: the space itself is opened.
A named section is always taken.
A record reference opens its space, and the record’s own page in it.
A reference naming only a space opens the space.
A reference naming a person goes nowhere.
A template’s declared panels, untouched: no instances opened beyond them.
Closing a declared panel opens or closes no instance; the arrangement it changes is layout’s.
Putting a closed declared panel back.
Another instance of a declared panel, with what it was opened with.
The same inputs again bring the open instance forward rather than opening a second.
Closing an instance by the id the host gave it, read from panelInstances.
Scrolling is not state: nothing a profile reads changes.
A template’s declared panels as it arranged them: nothing moved, no lane folded.
Closing a declared panel is a change to the arrangement the template declared.
Putting the only closed panel back leaves the arrangement as the template declared it.
Folding a lane away.
Toggling a folded lane brings it back.
Folding a lane as said rather than flipped.
Saying a folded lane is folded changes nothing.
Unfolding a folded lane, as said.
Reset puts back every declared panel and unfolds every lane.
Resetting what nobody moved changes nothing.
A clock named for the first time, given a range.
Playing from no moment starts at the range’s start. Time does not pass in a case.
With no range to cross, play does nothing.
Pausing stops the clock where it is.
Toggling a stopped clock plays it.
Seeking shows a moment, kept inside the range.
A moment may be given as an ISO date.
null shows everything again.
A fraction of the way through the range.
Speed is a multiple of the clock’s own pace.
Looping is a setting the clock reports.
Who is here: everyone present in the space on screen, the viewing person included, and who is on this page.
A personal space has nobody to be present to.
The status said with this person’s presence.
Invisible stops saying anything.
Saying what this person is doing.
An activity of the same type and id replaces the one said before.
Withdrawing one activity by type and id.
With no id, every activity of that type.
Moving to another page changes who shares it.
Profiles as people published them, who is in the space, whom this person muted and what they read.
Somebody who published no name is still named: the name is assembled and never empty.
Another space on screen, other members; the person’s own mutes and read markers go with them.
The space on screen, whether this person may change it, its defaults and this person’s settings.
Outside a space there is no space, and nothing to administer.
Making a chosen picture into what the record stores changes nothing: writing it is the space’s operation.
Hiding a section for this person only: the space keeps it, navigation drops it.
Showing a hidden section again.
Hiding a module for this person only.
This person’s own value decides over the space’s.
With no value, this person’s own is withdrawn and the next level decides again.
In a space: its own template and theme on offer beside this person’s, under a template the host brings that brings a theme of its own.
Outside a space nothing of a space is on offer, and what is on screen is the host’s for this person.
Switching to the space’s own template, by its switcher row.
Choosing to see the space’s own template here, over a default that names none, as this person alone.
The second option follows this person’s own default template here — the host’s, in this world — under which the space’s own theme shows.
A theme of this person’s own, chosen for the space on screen: shown, and a choice there is to undo.
Under a template that brings its own theme, choosing the space’s is a choice of its own, and one there is to undo.
Withdrawing the choice shows what showed before it.
Choosing a theme for the space by its override option, as a picker does.
The second option follows this person’s own default theme here, whatever the space’s is: the host’s, in this world.
